seoTitle: Michigan Distracted Driving Accident Lawyer – Hands-Free Law
seoDescription: Hit by a driver on their phone in Michigan? Since 2023, holding a phone while driving is illegal. ATLAW explains how the violation proves fault and how phone records are obtained. Free review.
tagline: Michigan’s hands-free law made holding a phone behind the wheel a violation. Here is how that violation proves your case, and how the phone records are obtained before they disappear.
secondaryKeywords: texting and driving accident lawyer michigan

c.v: In 2024, 14,439 crashes in Michigan involved a distracted driver. They killed 65 people and injured more than 5,400. Those are the crashes where the officer recorded distraction; the real number is higher, because a driver who was texting rarely admits it at the scene. What has changed since June 30, 2023, is that holding a phone while driving is itself a violation of Michigan law, and the phone company keeps the record that shows whether the driver was using it. A distracted driving case is a car accident case with evidence that can help establish how the crash happened and who was responsible, if someone goes and gets it.

Michigan’s hands-free driving law (MCL 257.602b, effective June 30, 2023) prohibits a driver from holding or using a mobile electronic device while operating a vehicle on a public road, including while stopped at a light. “Using” covers making or receiving a call, sending or reading a text or email, watching or recording video, using social media, and entering information into an app or navigation system by hand.

What is allowed: hands-free use through voice commands or a single touch to start or end a call, a device mounted on the dash or windshield, and use to call 911 or report an emergency. Commercial vehicle and school bus drivers are held to a stricter standard.

Penalties (MCL 257.602b(6)): a first violation is a $100 fine and/or 16 hours of community service; a second or later violation is $250 and/or 24 hours. The fines double if the driver was at fault in a crash while violating the law. Three violations in three years require a driver improvement course. For commercial drivers the fines are $200 and $500.
Kelsey’s Law

(MCL 257.602c) goes further for teen drivers: a driver on a Level 1 or Level 2 graduated license may not make, answer, or participate in phone calls while driving, including hands-free calls, subject to statutory emergency exceptions. Other device use remains governed by the hands-free law.

The law changed Michigan from a state that banned only texting (the 2010 law) to a state that bans holding the phone. That matters for an injury case: before 2023, a lawyer had to prove the driver was texting as opposed to dialing. Now, holding the phone is enough.

sections.heading: How a hands-free violation proves your case

c.v: In a negligence case, you have to prove the other driver failed to use reasonable care. Michigan treats the violation of a safety statute as evidence of negligence: when a driver breaks a law designed to prevent exactly the kind of harm that occurred, the jury may find negligence from the violation itself. A driver cited under the hands-free law, or shown by phone records to have been using the phone at the moment of the crash, has very little to argue about on fault. The case then turns on the injury and its value.

The crash report (UD-10).

sections.heading: How Michigan no-fault applies to a distracted driving crash

c.v: Distracted driving changes who is at fault; it does not change how no-fault works. The responsible PIP insurer pays eligible medical expenses under Michigan’s priority rules and the applicable coverage, and 85% of your lost wages (up to $7,455 a month for crashes on or after October 1, 2026), regardless of fault. A PIP lawsuit generally must begin within one year unless timely written injury notice or a previous PIP payment permits later filing, subject to additional filing and recovery limits (MCL 500.3145). To recover for pain and suffering and for economic losses beyond no-fault, you sue the distracted driver, and you may if your injury is a serious impairment of body function (MCL 500.3135). The driver’s violation makes the fault element of that lawsuit close to certain, which in practice means a higher settlement than the same injury with disputed fault.

Comparative fault still applies: if you were more than 50% at fault you cannot recover non-economic damages. A distracted driver’s insurer will look for distraction on your side too, which is a reason not to volunteer your own phone use to an adjuster.

If the distracted driver was working (a delivery driver, a rideshare driver, a company vehicle), the employer may be liable as well, and commercial drivers are subject to the stricter federal and Michigan rules. If the driver was a teen on a graduated license, Kelsey’s Law applies, and the parents’ policy may provide coverage, depending on its terms and whether it covers the teen and the vehicle.

Michigan’s distraction crashes in 2024 by type of distraction, from the State Police: 14.5% involved a cell phone, 10.6% another electronic device, 5.3% a passenger, 36.3% another activity inside the vehicle (eating, reaching, adjusting controls), and 33.3% an activity outside the vehicle (rubbernecking, looking at something on the road). The cell phone share is understated, because it depends on the driver admitting it or the officer observing it.

The four counties ATLAW serves recorded 118,110 crashes in 2024, with 34,424 people injured and 350 killed. The rear-end crash on Telegraph, Ford Road, Van Dyke, Gratiot, or I-94 at a slowdown is the classic distracted driving crash, and the three intersections with the most crashes in Michigan in 2024 (18½ Mile at Van Dyke in Sterling Heights, 11 Mile at Van Dyke in Warren, Telegraph at 12 Mile in Southfield) are all signalized intersections where a driver looking down misses the light.

faqs.question: Is it illegal to hold a phone while driving in Michigan?

answer.v: Yes, since June 30, 2023 (MCL 257.602b). Holding or using a phone for calls, texts, video, social media, or manual navigation entry is a civil infraction: $100 and/or 16 hours of community service for a first offense, $250 and/or 24 hours after that, doubled if the driver was in a crash.

faqs.question: How do I prove the other driver was on their phone?

answer.v: The crash report’s distraction code, the driver’s statements, witnesses, and, once suit is filed, the carrier’s call and data records obtained by subpoena and matched to the crash time. A preservation letter sent early keeps the phone itself from being wiped.

faqs.question: Can I get the other driver’s phone records myself?

answer.v: No. Carriers release records only to the account holder or under subpoena. A lawyer obtains them after filing the lawsuit.

faqs.question: Does a hands-free ticket mean the driver is automatically at fault?

answer.v: Not automatically, but close. Violation of a safety law is evidence of negligence in Michigan, and a ticket plus records showing use at the moment of the crash leaves little to dispute.

faqs.question: What if the driver was a teenager?

answer.v: Kelsey’s Law (MCL 257.602c) bars drivers on Level 1 and 2 graduated licenses from any phone use, including hands-free. The teen’s parents’ policy covers the claim.

faqs.question: What if the distracted driver was working?

answer.v: The employer may be liable for a driver using a phone on the job, and commercial drivers face stricter rules. Delivery, rideshare, and company-vehicle crashes are investigated for employer liability.

faqs.question: Does no-fault still pay my bills if the other driver was texting?

answer.v: Yes. Your own insurer pays PIP regardless of fault. The distracted driver is liable for pain and suffering and for losses no-fault does not cover.
Michigan does not allow punitive damages in negligence cases. The driver’s conduct bears on the jury’s assessment of your non-economic damages, but there is no separate penalty award.
One year to notify your no-fault insurer, three years to sue the driver. The phone and camera evidence should be preserved within days.
